stem: Why may a hospital use respiratory-symptom screening or related entry measures for visitors during periods of increased community respiratory-virus activity?

options.A: To identify only bacterial infections because viral respiratory illnesses are not relevant to visitor infection-control measures.
options.B: To replace hand hygiene, source control, ventilation, and other infection-prevention measures in the facility.
options.C: To help identify potentially infectious visitors and reduce introduction or spread of respiratory pathogens as one component of layered infection prevention.
options.D: To permanently exclude all visitors because visitor precautions cannot be adjusted to symptoms, transmission conditions, or facility risk assessment.

rationale: Current CDC healthcare guidance uses layered measures to reduce respiratory-virus transmission. During periods of increased community respiratory-virus activity, facilities may use rapid screening/triage approaches, and visitors with respiratory symptoms should be advised about source control and encouraged to defer non-urgent routine visits until recovered. Screening is therefore one component of infection prevention, not a replacement for hand hygiene, source control, environmental controls, or other measures. C is the best answer.
educational_objective: Explain that visitor respiratory-symptom screening helps identify potentially infectious persons and supports layered prevention of respiratory-pathogen introduction and transmission in healthcare settings.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Preventing Transmission of Viral Respiratory Pathogens in Healthcare Settings
source_locator: 1. Optimize the Use of Administrative and Engineering Controls — rapid screening during increased community respiratory-virus activity; 2. Communicate About Recommended Infection Control Practices — visitors with respiratory symptoms should defer non-urgent routine visits; 3. Respiratory Hygiene/Cough Etiquette
source_claim_supported: Healthcare facilities may use screening/triage and visitor symptom guidance during periods of increased community respiratory-virus activity as part of layered measures to reduce viral respiratory transmission.

source_original.stem: Why may a hospital screen visitors for respiratory symptoms during periods of increased community respiratory illness?

options.A: To identify only bacterial infections because viral respiratory illnesses are not relevant to visitor screening
options.B: To replace hand hygiene, source control, ventilation, and other infection-prevention measures in the facility
options.C: To reduce introduction and spread of respiratory pathogens as one part of layered infection prevention
options.D: To permanently exclude all visitors because symptom screening cannot be adjusted to community transmission

source_original.rationale: CDC advises healthcare facilities to use layered respiratory infection-prevention practices. Visitors with respiratory symptoms should be advised about source control and may be encouraged to defer non-urgent visits until recovered.
source_original.source_detail: Visitor and respiratory hygiene recommendations; current healthcare guidance accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Kept the layered-prevention construct but changed 'screen visitors' to the more precise CDC-supported 'screening or related entry measures,' tied the rationale to the May 2025 CDC healthcare page, and preserved easy difficulty.

audit_findings.source_authority: CDC current healthcare respiratory-virus guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: CDC page dated 2025-05-21 and current on 2026-08-16.
audit_findings.claim_audit: CDC directly supports rapid symptom screening/triage during increased community activity and symptom-based visitor source control/deferment as part of multiple control measures.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect; CDC guidance specifically targets viral respiratory infections.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect; screening is one layer and does not replace hand hygiene/source control/environmental controls.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect; guidance is adaptable to symptoms, community activity and facility risk assessment rather than permanent exclusion.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C accurately states the preventive purpose without overstating screening as a standalone intervention.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives answer the purpose of visitor entry measures; no second plausible answer remains.
audit_findings.blueprint: NCSBN p.8 infection-prevention and care-environment content.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read the May 2025 CDC healthcare guidance and core practices, challenged whether active screening is universally required, narrowed the stem accordingly, and confirmed C remained uniquely correct.
